description.p: Leyen keeps a library of Windows games and runs them with Proton through umu-launcher, each in its own Wine prefix or in one shared with its group.

MangoHud, Wayland, WoW64, NTSync and HDR switches
Every game sandboxed: it reaches its prefix, its own folder and nothing else of your files
Winetricks components, the Wine configuration and the registry editor for any prefix
Menu entries that start a game from the desktop, and a command line to list, run and stop games

description.p: A game can no longer reach outside its sandbox through the folder that stands in for its cache: it could swap that folder for a link to your home directory and be handed all of it on its next launch. That folder is read-only inside the sandbox now, and a prefix that is your home directory, or holds it, is refused like any other folder that would undo the sandbox.

The daemon stays on the session bus when a game prints a NUL byte, and exits if it loses the bus rather than running on beside a second one. A game whose deletion the daemon refuses keeps its icon and menu entry, a game launched again right after it ends keeps its output in the log, and a settings file that cannot be read is reported in the log instead of being replaced by the defaults in silence. The window does less work on its own thread, frees a dialog with a shared folder when it closes and redraws Running Games from the daemon's updates, and leyen list piped into head ends quietly.

Every game runs in a sandbox now, and so does everything else that runs Windows code: the Wine configuration, the registry editor, a program run by hand and a dependency install. A program reaches its Wine prefix, the game folder named in its settings and the folders shared with it, and nothing else of your files; where the sandbox cannot be built, the launch is refused instead of running unconfined. Two settings come with it, at the preferences, the group and the game: extra folders to share, each read-only unless switched writable, and network access.

Because the game folder is the one folder of yours a game sees, it is required and set by hand, so games in a library from an earlier version need it filled in before they launch again. GameMode is gone, switch and setting: it cannot work from inside the sandbox, and keeping a game outside it would let the game signal every program you run. bubblewrap and unprivileged user namespaces are requirements from here on.

Games that share a prefix still share one wineserver, so three windows of one game keep each other's registry writes. The Proton log is written into the prefix, where it can be read after the game exits. The interface is translated into Russian. On NixOS the sandbox builds and the prefix's process namespace starts.

A dependency installed into a prefix that does not exist yet no longer counts the whole Wine installation as its own files, so removing it, or a failed install, leaves the prefix alone. Removing a component keeps the DLL overrides another installed component set too, and removes the overrides winetricks set, which were left behind. Reinstalling a winetricks component works again, the first install waits for winetricks to finish downloading, and the dependency manager waits for installs that take longer than five minutes, such as .NET.

A failed download says why, and a failed installer ends its message with the last lines of its output instead of all of it. A font installed again after All Fonts keeps All Fonts from being removed before it. A group title with an ampersand shows in the game dialog, and a menu entry is written only for a game ID Leyen gave.

A launch whose first command cannot start, such as a wrapper in the launch arguments that is not installed, no longer shows as running for good. Stopping a game signals only that game's processes, even beside one with a similar executable name on the same prefix, and a game's output keeps reaching the log when it prints text that is not UTF-8.

Wine Configuration, the Registry Editor and programs run in a prefix are tracked by the daemon: while they, or anything they started, run, no game starts on that prefix and no dependency is installed or removed, and what they print is in the log. Cancelling a dependency install stops every process it started, Wine's server included. Installing dependencies needs the systemd user session, as launching games does.

The umu-launcher and winetricks that Leyen downloads are releases pinned in it, refused unless their SHA-256 matches. The log file is readable by you alone, icons are read faster from executables that carry many images, and editing a group updates its menu entries in one pass.

The window is rebuilt with GTK 4.22 and libadwaita 1.9. A group opens as a page of its own that the back button, Escape or a swipe leave, and the library is updated in place, so it no longer flickers or jumps when a game starts or stops. Icons are larger and centred in their rows, and a logo on a transparent background is shown whole instead of cropped. Search filters what is loaded as it is typed and says when nothing matches, Enter launches the game under the keyboard, and screen readers name every row. The log follows new lines smoothly while it is at the end and stays where it was scrolled to.

Adding and editing share one dialog for games and one for groups, which cannot add the same game twice. The prefix tools are rows, the menu entry of a game is a switch, and the dependency manager takes typing straight away, clears it and then goes back on Escape, and says which components need the one about to be removed. Deleting a group says how many games go with it, and a game that is running cannot be deleted, nor a group with one running.

The application id is io.github.sachesi.leyen; icons and menu entries written under the old id are moved over on the first start. Ctrl+Q quits, Ctrl+W closes a window, and errors from the session bus read as a sentence about the daemon. Installing no longer stops a daemon that is tracking games, and the Ukrainian translation covers every new string of the interface.

Winetricks components install again over an earlier attempt, removing one takes it out of the prefix's record, catalogue entries run the verbs winetricks knows them by, and DLL overrides are written to the registry instead of only being noted. A game is told apart from its neighbours by its GAMEID, a download that fails stops the others it was started with, and runtimes are unpacked beside their destination before they replace it.

The window survives a restart of the daemon and no longer rebuilds the library every few seconds while a game runs. The add and edit dialogs have a title, and a group can be edited from the header while it is open.

Downloaded runtimes are checked against their digests and winetricks is pinned to a known release. The files Leyen keeps carry a version of their format, no more than four dependency jobs run at once, and a launch can no longer slip in twice while the first is being registered. Menu entries of games with the same name no longer overwrite each other, and a background task that crashes no longer leaves the window waiting on it.

Files are read and written away from the thread drawing the window. A dependency job and a launch no longer run against the same prefix at once, a session is removed only once its playtime is saved, and "leyen list" shows a running game that is no longer in the library.
The library keeps its scroll position when it is refreshed.

Games are started and tracked by a daemon on the session bus, which the window and the command line talk to. It exits when it has nothing to do, writes the library and the settings so that a crash cannot leave them half written, and reports why an operation failed. Dependency downloads can be cancelled, and the log window follows new lines as they come.
